prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer initially positioned face-down within arm's reach (0.1 to 0.5 m) of a grassy ground plane in frames 1 to 3, where brighter pixels at the upper-left and darker pixels at the lower-right capture the steep downward tilt of the turf. In frames 4 and 5, as the camera rolls 90 degrees onto its side and pulls back slightly, the brightest near region shifts to the right side of the frame (0.2 to 0.5 m, within arm's reach) while the lawn recedes toward the left background. At the upper-left of frames 4 and 5, a resting sports helmet about 1.0 to 1.5 m away (just beyond or at the limit of arm's reach, partly cut off at the top edge in frame 4) appears as a distinct medium-grey volume protruding above the darker receding grass, with a small object directly behind it in frame 5 and tiny distant figures 15 to 30 m away along the far-left horizon. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates individual overlapping grass blades even during heavy motion blur in frame 3 and sharply traces the 3D relief of the helmet's wire face grille facing toward the lower-right. However, the map is unreliable across frame transitions because per-frame depth normalization makes the distant sky, buildings, and far people on the left edge of frame 5 collapse into uniform black without metric differentiation from the mid-ground turf.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely blank across frames 1 to 3, where only close-up grass (0.1 to 0.5 m in front of the camera wearer, within arm's reach) fills the view and no discrete foreground objects or people are present. In frames 4 and 5, as the camera turns sideways and tilts slightly further back, a single pink mask labeled 'person' appears at the upper-left, about 1.0 to 1.5 m from the camera wearer, expanding downward and leftward as more of the object enters the frame after being partially cropped at the top border in frame 4. Using the RGB context, this mask actually outlines a blue-and-white sports helmet resting on the grass (with its open grille oriented toward the bottom-right) along with a small pink item immediately behind it in frame 5, rather than an actual human facing or looking toward the camera wearer. While the mask provides a crisp silhouette of the solid helmet shell against the visually busy grass, it is highly unreliable semantically and spatially: it misclassifies an inanimate helmet as a person, omits the helmet's thin wire faceguard that extends to the right, and completely misses the real distant people standing 15 to 30 m away (several metres apart from each other and facing across the field) near the left horizon in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map is entirely black across all five frames, detecting no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand keypoints anywhere in the sequence. Spatial context from the RGB strip confirms that in frames 1 to 3 the camera is pointed directly into the grass at 0.1 to 0.5 m (within the camera wearer's reach, though the wearer's own hands and body remain out of view), and in frames 4 and 5 the object at the upper-left (1.0 to 1.5 m away) is an empty helmet on the turf rather than a person. What the pose map contributes beyond the segmentation map is confirmation that no close-range human body or head orientation is present at the upper-left of frames 4 and 5, correcting the false 'person' mask in the segmentation output. However, the pose map provides no scene layout information on its own and is unreliable at long range and under extreme 90-degree camera roll, failing to detect the distant people standing 15 to 30 m away along the far-left edge of frame 5 who are sideways in the image and not looking toward the camera wearer.
